proposals.old:
have hs : ∀ {l₁ l₂ : Ident} {a₁ a₂ : Aexp},
          l₁ ≠ l₂ →
          VarNotUsedInAexp l₁ a₂ →
          VarNotUsedInAexp l₂ a₁ →
          ∀ {st st' : State},
            (st =[ l₁ := a₁; l₂ := a₂ ]=> st') →
            st =[ l₂ := a₂; l₁ := a₁ ]=> st' := by
        intro l₁ l₂ a₁ a₂ hneq hne₁ hne₂ st st' h
        inversion h with
proposals.new:
have hs {l₁ l₂ : Ident} {a₁ a₂ : Aexp} (hneq : l₁ ≠ l₂)
          (hne₁ : VarNotUsedInAexp l₁ a₂)
          (hne₂ : VarNotUsedInAexp l₂ a₁) {st st' : State}
          (h : st =[ l₁ := a₁; l₂ := a₂ ]=> st') :
          st =[ l₂ := a₂; l₁ := a₁ ]=> st' := by
        inversion h with
proposals.why: LF/Basics.lean's "Displaying Theorem Statements" section establishes declaration-header style (named binders before the colon) as the book's convention; this internal `have` instead quantified its hypotheses with `∀`/`→` and then `intro`'d them by hand, exactly the pattern the convention replaces.
